- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.5) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 2–5% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a 1–2 day lag correction by reducing forecast slope.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 30-day horizon; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–2σ; if below, increase by 1–2σ.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment ≤ 0.2 for 5+ days), model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to counteract complacency.
- If model forecast is consistently 2–3% higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward bias to next forecast.
